items.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I wanted so desperately to play with him... So that night I go to Denver to meet the band from California.

ctx.x: So you already knew—you were familiar with his music so you didn’t have any apprehensions about playing Monk’s music?
No. I mean Coltrane was working with him during that period. So that was the first time I heard Coltrane play.

items.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Well I remember we played “My Favorite Things”... and all the rest of the stuff that we recorded that day

ctx.x: Well I remember we played “My Favorite Things” because when we got back and went to New York after that and into the studio to record it; and all the rest of the stuff that we recorded that day: “Mr. Day” and “Mr. Night” and all those tunes.
Do you recall Trane of McCoy saying anything to you at that gig or after the gig? How was your feeling after playing that gig?
I felt good. You know no one talked to me and I didn’t talk to anybody. We were like the Budapest String Quartet! (Laughs)

items.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Can you recall what happened in the session, in the Duke Ellington John Coltrane session?... I was on, let’s see, two tracks or three.

ctx.x: Can you recall what happened in the session, in the Duke Ellington John Coltrane session? How that came about and your recollections about it?

He just got into the studio and Duke, he’s a very…he’s a warrior in that sense. He sat at the piano, he did a couple things, and Coltrane was warming up. The next thing we do is we’re playing this (Elvin scats a melody) that was his little ditty. And I thought it was a lot of fun. I was on, let’s see, two tracks or three.
